home.heading: Embodied Brain Lab (EBL)
paragraphs: The EBL focuses on agent driven embodied brain research on robotics, UAV, and other unmanned systems, and other fields, such as Physical AI, Agentic AI, AI4Engr, etc.

research.title: Embodied Robotics
research.description: Imitation learning and perception-action methods for robotic tasks.

research.title: Aerial Embodied Intelligence
research.description: Visual and spatial reasoning for aerial vision-language navigation, including environment understanding and instruction following.

research.title: Agentic AI for Robotics
research.description: Multimodal large models for robotic navigation and decision-making, including frameworks for autonomous learning and improvement.

news.text: Professor Xiaoguang Ma presented research on autonomous learning and evolution in embodied navigation at Tianjin University's Beiyang Intelligent Computing Forum.
Professor Xiaoguang Ma was invited to the Beiyang Intelligent Computing Forum to give a talk on the transition from physical intelligence to embodied intelligence.

publications.title: ViSA-Enhanced Aerial VLN: A Visual-Spatial Reasoning Enhanced Framework for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
publications.abstract: A triple-phase architecture uses structured visual prompting so that vision-language models can reason directly on image planes for aerial VLN, without extra training or intermediate scene graphs. On the CityNav benchmark it improves the success rate by 70.3% over the fully trained state of the art.

publications.title: SE-VLN: A Self-Evolving Vision-Language Navigation Framework Based on Multimodal Large Language Models
publications.venue: ACSAT 2026 (as listed on the school website) · arXiv:2507.13152
publications.abstract: The first multimodal LLM-powered self-evolving VLN framework, which keeps evolving during testing through hierarchical memory, retrieval-augmented reasoning, and reflection. It achieves 57% and 35.2% success rates in unseen environments on R2R and REVERSE, surpassing current state-of-the-art methods.
publications.note: The preprint was first released in 2025. This page lists it under 2026 based on the conference information on the school website.

publications.title: Subconscious Robotic Imitation Learning
publications.abstract: Mimics subconscious-driven habitual actions through intent-aware sampling and hierarchical cognitive reasoning, allowing dual-arm robots to execute imitation-learning tasks 100% to 200% faster than state-of-the-art policies while keeping consistently higher success rates.

publications.title: M3DSS: A Multi-Platform, Multi-Sensor, and Multi-Scenario Dataset for SLAM System
publications.abstract: A multi-platform, multi-sensor, and multi-scenario SLAM dataset of 55 sequences recorded by a handheld rig, an unmanned ground vehicle, a quadruped robot, a car, and a UAV. Its 21 sensors include stereo event cameras, infrared and RGB cameras, five LiDARs, three IMUs, and RTK GNSS/INS, covering extreme illumination, aggressive motion, low texture, and high-speed driving, together with a benchmark of state-of-the-art SLAM systems.

publications.title: Frefusion: Frequency Domain Transformer for Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
publications.abstract: The first study of image fusion from a frequency-domain perspective: a frequency-domain feature extraction module, a frequency-domain Transformer that merges the features, and a residual reconstruction module produce the fused image. On MSRS, TNO, and Roadscene it outperforms several state-of-the-art fusion methods, showing potential as a generic backbone for visible and infrared image fusion.

teachers.name: Xiaoguang Ma
teachers.role: Peiyang Chair Professor · School of Artificial Intelligence, Tianjin University
teachers.bio: Xiaoguang Ma serves as a Peiyang Chair Professor at the School of Artificial Intelligence, Tianjin University, and is a Standing Committee Member of the CCF Technical Committee on Intelligent Robotics and of the CAAI Technical Committee on Human-Machine Integration. His research covers agent-driven Physical AI, AI4Engr, and unmanned systems.
